items.claim: The single-verse cut at the chazon superscription is warranted: 1:1 is a self-contained header naming the seer, patronym, object, and four-king window with no imperative or address of its own, and 1:2 opens a fresh, unrelated imperative summons.
items.evidence: 1:1's header content (seer, patronym, Judah/Jerusalem object, four-king regnal window) has no counterpart in 1:2, which opens with a heaven/earth imperative-vocative pair naming no king; the cut matches the owner-ruled F1 frame (Isa.1.1-Isa.1.1) exactly and the closed-vocabulary superscription value.

items.claim: Isolating 1:2-3 as a witness-summons unit ahead of the hoy-onset indictment at 1:4 is grounded in a genuine tier-1 frame shift, not an arbitrary cut.
items.evidence: 1:2 opens with a double imperative-vocative addressed to heaven and earth as legal witnesses; 1:4 opens with the book's tier-1 hoy-onset marker beginning a description of the nation's condition, giving the row's closing seam an independent frame signal rather than a mid-sentence break.
tier_citations: tier-1 frame classification, oshb:Isa.1.4 hoy onset

items.claim: Classifying 1:4's hoy as an opening indictment rather than a woe-oracle onset matches the book's own role-split for that exact verse, and the row's closing seam at 1:9/1:10 is doubly corroborated.
items.evidence: 1:4's hoy targets the nation's condition in general description rather than pronouncing doom on a named target-class, the same distinction the book-wide device inventory draws for this verse; a setumah break closes 1:9 (tier-3, single witness) and 1:10 independently opens a fresh imperative-vocative pair naming a new addressee, so the seam carries both a tier-3 and a tier-1 signal.
tier_citations: tier-3 parashah SAMEKH, oshb:Isa.1.9, single witness

items.claim: The 1:10 imperative reopening is a genuine tier-1 addressee shift, and the row correctly reads the Sodom/Gomorrah repetition across 1:9/1:10 as a rhetorical pivot rather than as proof the seam should not exist.
items.evidence: 1:10 redeploys the shema/azan verb pair of 1:2 but redirects it, in different verb forms, at a new plural human addressee named via the Sodom/Gomorrah comparison just introduced in 1:9; a setumah break also closes 1:17 (tier-3), and 1:18 independently opens with its own first-person divine invitation formula, giving the row's closing seam a tier-1 basis beyond the tier-3 corroboration.
tier_citations: tier-3 parashah SAMEKH, oshb:Isa.1.17, single witness

items.claim: Isolating 1:18-20 rests on a genuine tier-1 speech-act shift (a first-person divine invitation formula) and a recognized oracle-closing signature, and the row names and rejects the strongest real rival on textual grounds rather than as a strawman.
items.evidence: 1:18 opens with a first-person divine invitation-to-reason formula distinct from the imperative catalogue of 1:16-17; 1:20 closes with the recognized mouth-of-Yahweh-has-spoken oracle-closing signature, corroborated by a tier-3 setumah break at the same verse; the rejected alternative, treating 1:18-20 as the conclusion of the preceding ritual critique in 1:10-17, is the natural rival and is answered on the formula-shift grounds rather than dismissed.
tier_citations: tier-3 parashah SAMEKH, oshb:Isa.1.20, single witness

items.claim: The skeleton-tier inclusio bracketing 1:21-26 is byte-verified exactly as disclosed, the internal 1:24 hoy/neum is correctly read as a divine self-exclamation and postpositive signature rather than a row-cutting seam, and the rival cut at 1:23/1:24 is genuinely disclosed and weighed rather than suppressed.
items.evidence: Direct collation of the source bytes confirms the city-designation phrase recurs at 1:21 and 1:26 with identical consonants but differing verse-final cantillation (a mid-verse disjunctive at 1:21 versus a verse-final accent at 1:26), matching the row's own skeleton-tier, not byte-identical, claim exactly; a petuchah break at 1:23 (tier-3, single witness) is disclosed as the strongest rival rather than hidden; 1:24's hoy interjection sits immediately after the divine title-and-signature stack, matching the book-wide classification of that verse as a self-exclamation over Yahweh's own action rather than a woe against the addressee.
tier_citations: byte-tier Hebrew collation, oshb:Isa.1.21 and oshb:Isa.1.26
tier-3 parashah PE, oshb:Isa.1.23, single witness

items.claim: The 1:26/1:27 cut is honestly built on a soft, non-tier-1 discourse-mode shift, held at correspondingly reduced confidence, and the row names and rejects the strongest rival, reading 1:21-31 as one unbroken unit, rather than ignoring it.
items.evidence: 1:27 shifts to third-person declarative summary from the first-person divine speech that runs through 1:24-26, a real but sub-tier-1 signal that the row explicitly discloses as its sole basis for the cut, calibrating confidence to medium_low accordingly rather than overclaiming; a setumah break independently closes the chapter at 1:31 (tier-3, single witness).
tier_citations: tier-3 parashah SAMEKH, oshb:Isa.1.31, single witness

items.claim: The 2:1 ha-davar header is correctly isolated as its own frame-exact superscription, symmetric to the 1:1 treatment, with an accurate, non-fabricated header-noun contrast and correct upstream tier-3 corroboration.
items.evidence: 2:1 opens with a header-noun distinct from 1:1's opening term while retaining the same seeing-verb and patronymic, a genuine lexical distinction rather than a copying variant; 2:2 opens a fresh eschatological formula closing the row's own seam; a setumah break independently closes 1:31 immediately upstream (tier-3, single witness), and the row's parent_collection and unit_type both match the owner-ruled architecture exactly.
tier_citations: tier-3 parashah SAMEKH, oshb:Isa.1.31, single witness
